newsitem.title: USA: Corrections to build Oklahoma prison.
newsitem.headline: Corrections to build Oklahoma prison.

text.p: Corrections Corp of America said Tuesday it agreed to build a 960-bed, medium- security prison in Sayre, Okla., to house adult male inmates for the state of Oklahoma.

The $29 million prison will be financed with tax-exempt bonds issued by the Sayre Industrial Authority, which has contracted with the company for the design, construction and operation of the facility.
After completion in February 1998, the prison is expected to generate over $11 million in annualized revenues.

"We are proud that our performance in Holdenville has made CCA an attractive alternative for meeting Oklahoma's prison bed needs," said chief executive Doctor R. Crants. "This represents the 13th new project that CCA has developed in 1996 and, with expansions of existing facilities, totals over 10,000 new beds under contract this year."
CCA manages the Davis Correctional Center in Holdenville, which opened last April, and will manage the Cimarron Correctional Facility in Cushing, when it opens in June 1997.
